sourceTheorem.title: Construction of a selfadjoint, strictly positive transfer matrix for Euclidean lattice gauge theories
sourceTheorem.locator: DESY 76/54, §II A–C, Proposition 1 and Proposition 2; equations (17), (20)–(23), (28)–(30)
sourceTheorem.sourceScope: SU(N), Wilson action, normalized Haar links; periodic spatial and temporal gauge boundaries. Pure-gauge factor obtained by omitting the fermion factor.

value.required: A finite product of normalized Haar measures, including the temporal-link gauge projector.

assumptions.source: Positive coefficients of the character expansion in the proof of Proposition 1
Proposition 2 periodic case; the open case uses the explicit equal boundary vector in the derivation below

value.required: Finite gauge-invariant polynomials in link matrix coefficients and their conjugates supported in the positive-time half, followed by the L² closure.

reflection.boundaryState: Periodic gauge trace, Z proportional to Tr(T^Nt)

reflectionPositivity.antilinearMap: (Theta F)(U)=conjugate(F(theta U)); a reversed oriented link is represented by its inverse.

operator.space: H_phys=P_G L²(G^E,dHaar), with E the active spatial links; generally infinite-dimensional.
operator.gaussProjector: (P_G f)(U)=integral_{G^vertices} f((Omega_x U_xy Omega_y^-1)_edges) dOmega; P_G=P_G*=P_G².
operator.spatialMultiplier: M f=exp(-S_spatial/2) f; M is bounded, positive, gauge invariant and invertible at a finite beta.
operator.kineticKernel: K(U,V)=product_edges k_beta_t(U_e V_e^-1), k_b(g)=exp[-b(1-Re chi_R(g)/dim R)]/z_b.
operator.transfer: T=M P_G K P_G M, up to a strictly positive scalar normalization from the temporal one-link integrals.
operator.strictPositivity: The faithful R and its conjugate generate every irreducible representation; all kinetic Fourier coefficients are positive. T is injective on H_phys.
operator.unitarity: Euclidean T is self-adjoint positive, not a unitary time evolution. For beta>0, H=-log(T)/a_t is defined by spectral calculus; real-time exp(-itH) is unitary.

derivation.identity: exp[c Re chi_R]=sum_{n,m>=0} (c/2)^(n+m)/(n!m!) chi_{R^tensor n tensor Rbar^tensor m}
derivation.reason: Every finite tensor product decomposes with nonnegative integer multiplicities. Compactness gives uniform absolute convergence, so all irreducible character coefficients of the kernel are nonnegative.

derivation.identity: <f,Kf>=sum_pi d_pi (a_pi/d_pi) ||fhat(pi)||_HS² >=0, with fhat(pi)=integral f(g) pi(g)* dg
derivation.reason: Peter–Weyl orthogonality diagonalizes a central convolution kernel. Tensor products over finitely many spatial links preserve positivity.
The temporal-link integral is the orthogonal gauge projector. Both K and M commute with the gauge action. Nonnegative anisotropic coefficients change these factors without changing this argument.

derivation.identity: Open reflection gives ||K^(1/2) P_G h_F||²/Z (link plane) or an integral of |h_F|²/Z (site plane). Periodic reflection gives Tr(A_F* A_F)/Z after splitting the positive transfer powers.
derivation.reason: The two halves have the same local action and Haar measure and are related by the displayed antilinear reflection. For open boundaries the two boundary vectors agree. These identities apply to the entire stated algebra, rather than a finite collection of numeric correlations.

reflectionPositivity.numericEvidenceRole: Finite correlation matrices or numerical eigenvalues are not the proof of this property.

transferOperator.hilbertSpace: Gauge-invariant subspace of L²(G^spatialEdges,dHaar), normally infinite-dimensional even for finitely many edges.

topologyDiagnostic.scope: Mobility of the explicitly measured unrounded plaquette/clover charge estimator. No certified integer-sector observable is available for rough links; sector mixing and topology conservation are not inferred by rounding.

cutoff.weightDefinition: sum_edges 2*j_e, with j_e a nonnegative half-integer
cutoff.gaussConstraint: At each trivalent cube vertex, SU(2) invariant tensors exist iff the three 2j values have even sum and satisfy all triangle inequalities. The intertwiner multiplicity is then one.
cutoff.orthonormality: Normalized product Haar measure and Peter–Weyl orthogonality give norm one to each fundamental closed-loop character. Distinct cube faces contain an edge occurring in only one character, so integrating that edge gives zero. The vacuum is orthogonal to every face.
cutoff.completeness: Every weight assignment with total weight <=5 was enumerated and checked against the exact trivalent Gauss rules. The surviving states are precisely the vacuum and the six fundamental face loops. No periodic or larger graph is substituted.
cutoff.basisDefinition: phi_0=1; phi_p=chi_(1/2)(ordered face holonomy)=Tr(U_p), not normalized trace.

cutoffProof.derivation: The positive Bessel series gives I_n<= (beta/2)^n/n! exp(beta²/[4(n+1)]), I_1>=beta/2, and n!>=2^(n-1). Every omitted physical assignment has total spin weight >=6, hence ||K(1-P_5)||<=q^6. Since ||M||<=1 and P_5 commutes with K, ||T-T_5||<=q^6.
cutoffProof.notUniformInContinuum: The bound belongs to this graph, beta_t, beta_s and cutoff. It may be uninformative at large beta.

cubature.rule: A simultaneous two-sided Hoeffding union bound for all 49 entries uses the exact ranges |phi_p|<=2 and 0<exp(-S)<=1. The weighted maximum row sum bounds the matrix operator norm.
cubature.qualification: The probability statement is conditional on ideal independent Haar draws. The finite pinned PRNG and Float64 Box–Muller generator simulate that model; a deterministic PRNG sequence is not a mathematical source of independent randomness.

errorBudget.numerics: Directed exponential and Bessel enclosures; conservative local quaternion/moment roundoff allowance, plus the accumulated binary64 sum bound. Numerical eigen residuals do not replace the analytic positivity argument.

transferOperator.fullOperator: T=M P_G K P_G M, M=exp(-S_spatial/2). K is normalized so its vacuum eigenvalue is one.
transferOperator.cutoffOperator: T_5=M P_5 K P_5 M, where P_5 keeps every physical spin-network of total sum(2j)<=5.
transferOperator.basisMap: X e_i=sqrt(lambda_i) M phi_i. T_5=X X*, and this 7×7 matrix approximates X* X=Lambda^(1/2) G Lambda^(1/2), G_ij=<phi_i,exp(-S_spatial)phi_j>. It is not the bare matrix of T in an orthonormal basis of M phi_i.

positivity.analytic: T_5 is positive since K has nonnegative character coefficients and T_5=X X*. Every cubature row has positive weight and contributes a positive outer product to the companion matrix.
positivity.lowerBoundScope: Exact finite cutoff companion X*X; the displayed empirical cubature spectrum has its separate total error budget.

unitarity.reason: Euclidean T is positive and contractive, so it is not a unitary group evolution.

finiteRealTimeEvolution.scope: Spectral evolution exp(-it H_hat) of this computed finite positive companion matrix only; projected link multiplication is not asserted to be unitary.

gaugeSymmetry.reason: Every retained spin-network satisfies the exact vertex Gauss constraint; multiplication by M is gauge invariant.

comparison.rule: The chain mean must lie in the independently constructed simultaneous Haar reference interval expanded by six autocorrelation-adjusted chain standard errors. The rule and failure probability are fixed before sampling.

The chain mean must lie in the independently constructed simultaneous Haar reference interval expanded by six autocorrelation-adjusted chain standard errors. The rule and failure probability are fixed before sampling.

bounds.proof: Distinct elementary plaquettes on this open, nondegenerate graph have zero Haar covariance: at least one link occurs in only one loop. Each normalized SU(2) fundamental trace has Haar variance 1/4. Thus E[(mean plaquette)^2]=1/(4 Np). For Y=exp(-S) mean plaquette, Var(Y)<=E[Y²]<=1/(4 Np), since 0<=exp(-S)<=1. The centered variable is bounded by 2. Bernstein gives sqrt(2 v L/N)+4L/(3N). Hoeffding applies to exp(-S) in [0,1]; a union bound uses L=log(4/delta).

reference.scope: Actual SU(2) Wilson links on the four-dimensional 2×2×2×2 open lattice, at the selected nonzero beta. No one-link system is substituted for this comparison.
reference.method: Independent product-Haar draws with Boltzmann importance weights; quaternion arithmetic is separate from the dense-matrix Markov implementation.
reference.probabilityQualification: The concentration inequality assumes ideal independent Haar draws. The pinned xorshift/Box–Muller implementation is a reproducible finite PRNG simulation of that law; it is not a deterministic proof of randomness.

reference.formula: U=cos(theta) I+i sin(theta) n·sigma; normalized Haar radial weight (2/pi) sin²(theta) dtheta, theta∈[0,pi].
reference.method: Independent one-dimensional angular Simpson quadrature of the exact SU(2) Haar measure.

checklist.detail: Ns, Nt, spatial/Euclidean-time spacing and boundaries, anisotropy, representation, physical extents, site count and continuous group degrees of freedom are distinct.
Oriented group products, inverse and empty paths use U_xy:y→x. Classical links retain ordered-midpoint approximation and refinement diagnostics.
Actual ordered plaquettes, arbitrary signed paths, identity, pure gauge and nontrivial central temporal holonomy fixtures.
Site-wise transformation recomputes every plaquette and the total action. M1 lawful-group adjacent telescoping theorem is reused with its historical audit; no new browser kernel execution.
Wilson real character for every shipped faithful group representation; basic invariant form determines bare coupling and anisotropic coefficients.

Actual full-Lie plaquette/clover curvature, energy and real charge converge as both spacings shrink. Independent analytic-derivative local fixtures and a fixed physical 4D box integral retain every source link/cell and directed error budgets. Observed clover order two is distinguished from the conservative order-one bound; real Q is never rounded into an integer certificate.

Every classical M1 link has separate source-specific midpoint/trapezoidal integration, source evaluation, matrix exponential truncation/roundoff, product and boundary errors. Exact rational group data determine each of the fourteen representation bounds. Local rho/a and fixed-volume refinements are checked against independent BPST primitives/densities; finite-path/window bounds are not exported as arbitrary continuum theorems.
Source allocation and JSON budgets checked before constructing arrays; raw links remain complete while x4 slice/stride changes only the observation hash.
The finite normalized Haar-product Gibbs measure has an explicit positive partition-function bound; underflow is recorded in log scale.
Full SU(2) Haar or symmetric full-basis Lie exponential random-scan Metropolis; target action difference and proposal symmetry are explicit.

Both real SU(2) proposal algorithms meet independent Bessel/Haar one-link references. A nonzero-beta full 2×2×2×2 open lattice is compared with separate quaternion product-Haar importance sampling, predeclared Bernstein/Hoeffding intervals and pure-gauge controls. Wrong distribution/action controls fail; other-group quantitative validation is not inferred from these fixtures.

Two starts pass recorded burn-in, acceptance, action/loop/real-topology, split-Rhat, segment/replica mean and ESS gates on the declared small reference fixture. Separate real-charge mobility diagnostics reject long stagnant histories. Inadequate short production examples remain PARTIAL; these finite diagnostic passes do not prove general thermal equilibrium or integer topological-sector mixing.
Per-observable autocorrelation window, tau_int, ESS and batch-mean cross-check; insufficient ESS and constant/stalled series do not receive a confidence interval.

Six explicit model/action/Haar/boundary/algebra hypotheses map to Lüscher 1977, §II, Propositions 1–2. Direct SU(N) periodic isotropic application is distinguished from the displayed compact-group/anisotropic/open-boundary derivation. Negative beta, arbitrary measure, gauge-variant algebra and extra action terms cannot receive an application status. Finite numeric PSD matrices are not the proof.

The infinite-dimensional gauge-invariant L² space is retained explicitly. The full SU(2) open spatial cube has an exhaustively enumerated total-spin-weight≤5 Gauss basis of seven states. Its positive Gram companion has separate deterministic omitted-spin, independent-Haar cubature and arithmetic errors; symmetry and finite real-time unitarity are checked. Unsupported graphs/cutoffs are rejected, and Euclidean transfer is not called unitary.
Group/action/beta/spacing/volume/boundary, algorithm, seed, starts, flow=null, retained sample hashes and final raw configurations are sealed; source versus observation revisions are distinct.

proofBoundary: Original finite classical/lattice, theorem-hypothesis and explicit-cutoff acceptance is implemented. Short or stalled chains can remain PARTIAL. No new Lean kernel run, general equilibrium/topological-sector theorem, continuum QFT construction or mass-gap proof is asserted.
